snr_correction.reason: labelled-MT SNR matched to human-annotated MT-34 GT: synth median 0.50 -> target 1.45; sweep scratchpad/snr_calib.py gives 1.36 at x3

length_prior_fix.reason: shipped length_range=(80,950) with length_log_mean=6.60 gave a median of 694 px and a degenerate 30 % pile-up on the upper clamp; 88.1 % of HTW GT lies below the lower clamp. Frame-level length scale + count coupling replaces it.
length_prior_fix.verified: fg 1.25-1.93 % across the shift range; covers htw p50 29 px and 585 p50 358 px

photometry_fix.reason: the calibrated base-height range straddles the 56.4 nm interference zero-crossing; contrast_floor preserves the sign, so crossed segments render at full strength in the WRONG polarity. Measured: flipped label length 12.0% synth vs 2.2-3.4% real.

provenance_wide_physics.why: the project's own standing rule (biased-corpus-domain-randomization) says the real corpus is a biased sample of an unknown experiment space, so PHYSICS priors must be randomised WIDE. An audit of the shipped calibration found several at x1.5-2.0: bundle_size 2-3, ina 0.7-1.1, psf_sigma 0.8-1.6, n_bend 1-2. Those are narrow for quantities that move with defocus, numerical aperture and preparation. This is a gap between the stated principle and the implementation, not a new idea.
provenance_wide_physics.supported_by: arms 44/45 replicated on two seeds, 8/8: NARROWING a prior onto a measured real statistic costs 0.02-0.04 headline F1. Widening was null against the shipped prior, so the evidence supports 'do not narrow' more strongly than 'widen more'.
provenance_wide_physics.method_note: widened symmetrically around the shipped band, never re-centred. Re-centring onto a real statistic is exactly the FIT that was measured to be harmful.
provenance_wide_physics.honest_prediction: null. The evidence says shipped ~ WIDE > FIT, so the shipped priors already sit in the good regime and widening further has no measurement behind it. The reason to run it is that the audit exposed a principle/implementation gap and the GPUs are idle.
